transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

No matter how many lists and reminders I use, I keep forgetting everyday work tasks and follow-ups, and it’s starting to seriously affect my job as a nurse. I've always tried to be meticulous, but lately, important things are just slipping through the cracks and I'm really worried about my reliability.
Did these attention and memory problems start in childhood, or are they a new change that began later in life?

They actually go all the way back to childhood, even though they've become much more of a struggle recently. Even in elementary school, I was constantly forgetting my homework, losing permission slips in my desk, and my mom had to sit right next to me just to keep my mind from drifting off during simple worksheets.
Do you also have trouble with restlessness, fidgeting, interrupting others, or acting before thinking, or is it mainly inattention and forgetfulness?

It’s almost entirely inattention and forgetfulness—I don't really get restless or impulsive, and I'm actually overly cautious and spend extra time rechecking my work. The only exception is that I do tend to talk too much and ramble when I'm giving shift reports, but the core issue is definitely just keeping track of details and organizing my tasks.
Before age 12, did teachers or family members often describe you as being very fidgety, unable to sit still, or interrupting/blurting things out, or was it mainly inattention and forgetfulness?

It was definitely mainly inattention and forgetfulness, as I was never really a fidgety or hyperactive kid. Back then, I was always losing permission slips in my desk and forgetting to bring my homework back to school. My mind drifted off so much that my mom had to sit right next to me just to get me through simple worksheets.
Do these attention and forgetfulness problems still happen in more than one setting, like at work and at home, and do they cause clear problems in your daily life?

Yes, they absolutely affect both. At work, my manager has formally flagged my reliability and I was recently passed over for a charge nurse role, which has been devastating. Even in my personal life, I have to rely on constant phone alarms and sticky notes just to keep from forgetting basic daily tasks and appointments.

Have you ever had a long-standing pattern of hyperactive or impulsive behaviors, such as needing to move constantly, interrupting others, blurting things out, or acting without thinking, especially since childhood?

No, I don't really relate to physical hyperactivity, impulsivity, or acting without thinking, either now or as a child when my struggles were strictly about drifting off and losing things. The only thing close to that is my tendency to overtalk and give way too much detail when I'm explaining things or giving shift reports. Other than that, I've never had those kinds of behaviors.
Have your attention problems been present since childhood and caused impairment in more than one setting, even without significant hyperactivity or impulsivity?

Yes, looking back, these issues definitely started in childhood even though I was never hyperactive or bouncing off the walls. Back then, I was just the quiet kid who constantly lost permission slips and needed my mom to sit right next to me to keep my mind from drifting. It affected school and home back then, and now it is severely impacting my nursing career.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview confirms a lifelong pattern of prominent inattention, forgetfulness, losing items, distractibility, and organizational difficulty beginning in childhood and causing impairment at work and home. However, the presentation is predominantly inattentive without clear hyperactivity/impulsivity, so the best fit from the provided options is F98.8 (other specified behavioral and emotional disorders with onset usually occurring in childhood and adolescence), with F90.0 considered as the main ADHD-related differential.
